# Oxygen saturation measured at admission

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Indicator ID | `neo_spo2_measured_admission` |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Status | Draft |
| Unit | Neonatal |
| Type | Process |
| Direction | Higher is better |
| Table | `qi.qi_neonatal_spo2_measured_on_admission`, one row per site and admission month |

## Definition

The share of neonatal admissions, on the full form, whose oxygen saturation was recorded as measured at admission (pulse oximetry).

## Numerator

Eligible admissions with oxygen saturation recorded as measured. Column: `spo2_measured`.

## Denominator

Full-form admissions (is_minimum = 0), on which the question is asked. Column: `eligible`.

## Exclusions

- Minimum records, on which the CIN form does not ask the question. They are counted in minimum_form.
- Records whose form type is not recorded. They are counted in form_type_not_recorded.
- Admissions without a usable admission date.

## Documentation completeness

The share of eligible admissions with the question answered, yes or no (spo2_recorded / eligible). Not documented counts as not measured.

## REDCap fields

`oxygen_saturation_measured`, `is_minimum`, `date_adm`, `hosp_id`

## Why it matters

Hypoxaemia is common in sick newborns and often missed on clinical signs alone. WHO recommends pulse oximetry to detect hypoxaemia and to guide oxygen therapy, so measuring saturation on admission is the first step to giving oxygen, and CPAP, to the babies who need it.
